editor.tooltip.user_settings.key_binding: Single keys have a primary and an alternate. Shortcuts have two sets of two keys: hold the first, press the second. Click a key, then press the new one; Escape cancels, right click clears it. Escape itself can't be bound. Press Save to keep them for next time.
runtime_editor.tooltip.tool.move: Move the entity being edited with the arrows (one axis) or the squares (two axes). Snaps to the grid; hold {key:rt_disable_snap} to ignore it. Shortcut: {key:rt_move_tool}
runtime_editor.tooltip.tool.rotate: Rotate the entity being edited with the rings, around its own axes. Snaps to 15 degrees; hold {key:rt_disable_snap} to ignore it. Shortcut: {key:rt_rotate_tool}
runtime_editor.tooltip.gravity_mode: Keeps the camera at eye height above the floor under it, where a play-mode camera with the same eye height would be. Click to open its settings; {key:rt_gravity_mode} toggles it.
runtime_editor.tooltip.gravity_mode.eye_: Height of the camera above the floor, the same as a Player Controller's Eye Height.
runtime_editor.tooltip.camera_speed: How fast the camera flies. {key:rt_speed_up} / {key:rt_speed_down} also change it, {key:rt_reset_speed} resets it. Ctrl+click to type a value.
runtime_editor.tooltip.entity_markers: White circles on every entity, so ones without a sprite, model or collider can be found. Click (or {key:rt_toggle_entity_markers}) to cycle: always shown, hidden behind walls, off.
$CONTEXT_WIREFRAME: Wireframe is only rendering the edges of things as lines (walls, entitites etc.)
runtime_editor.tooltip.steps: How much scrolling and texture dragging change things. The fine steps are used while {key:rt_fine_scroll} is held.
editor.tooltip.engine_settings.auto_save: How often the open level is saved in the background when it has unsaved changes. 0 turns auto save off.
editor.tooltip.engine_settings.vsync: Frame pacing of the game window (Play and the runtime editor). Vsync: locked to the monitor's refresh rate. Adaptive Vsync: the same, but doesn't wait when a frame is late. Off: uncapped. Applies from the next Play or runtime editor session.
runtime_editor.tooltip.history: Show or hide the list of recent edits. Click an entry to undo or redo up to it.

&Context_14: The sector that is to the sout of the wall when looking from a bird's eye view

&Context_15_a: UV offset of the wall texture
&Context_17: An entity, can also be called an object, is basically anything in the game world aside from walls and sectors. Same as Unity's Gameobject
entity.name: Name
entity.title: Entity
&Context_18: A component is a (figurative) box of information that can be attached to an entity. For example a Transform Component would store information about the entity's position & rotation. And a Rigidbody Component would store information about the entity's velocity
&Context_19: Transform stores information about the entity's position, rotation and other whereabouts such as the current sector it is in
&Context_20: Sprite is a 2D billboarded image that always faces the camera, like enemies in Doom 1993
&Context_22: An audio source is a component that stores information about an audio file like its length and volume
&Context_23: 2D Cartesian position is defined by two coordinates (x, y)
&Context_24: Height is the distance from the floor. (Relative to the current sector the entity is in) So a height of 10 means the entity is flying 10 units above the floor
&Context_25: Floor as in the stories of a building. So a transform.floor = 2 means the entity is at the 2nd floor
&Context_26: The index of the texture in the array texture
&Context_32: A script is a piece of code the user can write to add custom functionality
&Context_33: A player controller is a component that has built-in functionalities for player movement.
&Context_34: Y position of the camera relative to the floor's height
&Context_38: If no clip is on, the player will not collide with anything
editor.tooltip.component.player_controll: Make it less than 1.0 to reduce air control
&Context_40: If the distance of an object to the camera is smaller than camera.near_plane, it will not render
&Context_41: If the distance of an object to the camera is larger than camera.far_plane, it will not render
&Context_42: Is trigger means the collider will register collision detection, but will not do collision resolution
&Context_43: Short for: Axis Aligned Bounding Box
&Context_45: Length, width and height of the AABB box as in (x, y, z)
editor.tooltip.component.offset: Position relative to the entity's Transform, turned with its rotation. Lets several of these sit at different spots on one entity.
editor.tooltip.component.collider.offset: Position of the collider's bottom relative to the entity's Transform, multiplied by its Scale and turned with its rotation. Lets several colliders sit at different spots on one entity.
component.rigidbody.not_first: Only the entity's first Rigidbody simulates. Drag this one to the top of the component list to use it.
component.rigidbody.no_collider: This entity has no Collider, so this body won't collide with anything and falls through floors.
editor.tooltip.entity.component_drag: Drag onto another component of the same type to reorder. The first one is the one scripts get from entity.<component>.
&Context_46: A rigidbody is a component that stores information about the physics-related part of the entity. Such as its velocity & mass
&Context_47: If rigidbody.is_static = true then the object will not move
&Context_56: A model component draws a static 3D model file (.obj, .fbx, .gltf, ...) at the entity's transform. Its textures load automatically.
&Context_57: Shown next to a texture that is stored inside the model file itself.
&Context_58: Shown next to a texture or file the model refers to that could not be found on disk.
&Context_59: A flipbook component plays a sprite animation (.fpk file) by swapping the textures of one of the entity's sprites (or UI sprites, on a UI entity).
component.flipbook.no_sprite: This entity has no Sprite. Add one for the flipbook to show.
component.flipbook.missing_file: The flipbook file could not be loaded.
&Context_60: Followed by a frame name and the sprite sides (N, NE, ...) that frame has no texture for.
&Context_61: The flipbook editor edits .fpk sprite animation files. A frame is one picture of the animation, with a texture for each of the 8 directions.

settings.rendering.tooltip.sky.fallback_: Shown when the sky has no usable image, and through transparent parts of it

settings.rendering.tooltip.wall_contrast: Fake contrast so corners stay readable in even lighting: walls running along Z are lit this much brighter than their sector, walls along X this much darker, and angled walls blend in between. In sector light units (0-255); 0 turns it off.
settings.rendering.tooltip.texture_prese: Controls how textures are filtered when viewed nearby and at a distance.
Uses nearest-neighbor filtering without mipmaps. Produces very sharp pixels but may shimmer or create moire patterns at a distance.
Uses nearest-neighbor filtering with nearest mipmaps. Keeps pixels sharp while reducing distant shimmering and moire patterns.
Uses sharp nearest-neighbor filtering nearby with smooth transitions between mipmap levels at a distance.
Uses linear filtering and smooth mipmaps. Suitable for realistic, high-resolution textures.
Uses sharp nearest-neighbor filtering nearby with smoother mipmap transitions at a distance for a crunchy retro appearance.
Uses linear filtering and smooth mipmaps to create a soft, blurry low-resolution appearance similar to some Nintendo 64-era games.

editor.tooltip.sector.ceil_height: Height of the ceiling plane in world units.
editor.tooltip.sector.floor_height: Height of the floor plane in world units.
editor.tooltip.sector.floor_texture: Drag a texture from the Asset Browser, or double-click one there and click here.
editor.tooltip.sector.ceil_texture: Drag a texture from the Asset Browser, or double-click one there and click here.
editor.tooltip.sector.light_value: Light level applied to entities in this sector (0 = fully dark, 255 = full bright).
editor.tooltip.sector.delete: Permanently remove this sector from the map.
editor.tooltip.sector.copy: Copy this sector's properties into New Sector Properties, so the next sector you draw matches it. Uses the bottom floor and the first wall's textures and color.
editor.tooltip.wall.front_sector: Sector on the front (visible) side of this wall.
editor.tooltip.wall.back_sector: Sector on the back side – INVALID_ID for solid walls.
editor.tooltip.wall.texture: Drag a texture from the Asset Browser, or double-click one there and click here.
editor.tooltip.wall.texture_middle: Fills the wall's openings, where both sides are open space - fences, bars, windows. Transparent pixels show through. Empty draws nothing. Only portal walls have openings.
editor.tooltip.wall.middle_has_collision: The middle blocks the player and rigidbodies.
editor.tooltip.wall.middle_ignored_by_ra: Raycasts pass through the middle: script raycasts, line of sight, and clicking it in the runtime editor.
editor.tooltip.wall.color: RGBA tint multiplied over the wall texture.
editor.tooltip.wall.texture_offset: UV offset for scrolling or aligning the wall texture.
editor.tooltip.wall.texture_scale: UV scale of the wall (makes the texture zoom in or out)
editor.tooltip.wall.anchor.auto: Top edge, except the wall above a neighbour's ceiling, which uses its bottom edge. Doors and lifts carry their textures with them.
editor.tooltip.wall.anchor.top_edge: The texture is pinned to the top edge and moves with it.
editor.tooltip.wall.anchor.bottom_edge: The texture is pinned to the bottom edge and moves with it.
editor.tooltip.wall.anchor.world: The texture is pinned to world height 0 and never moves. Use it for door tracks and to line up neighbouring walls.
editor.tooltip.wall.delete: Remove this wall from the map.
editor.tooltip.entity.common.delete: Delete this entity from the level.
editor.tooltip.entity.snap_to_wall: Then right-click a wall to stick the entity to it. It can only slide along the wall and up or down, and always faces away from it.
editor.tooltip.entity.snap_to_wall_cance: Stop choosing a wall. Escape or right-clicking anything that isn't a wall does the same.
editor.tooltip.entity.disable_wall_snap: Let the entity move freely again. It stays where it is.
editor.tooltip.entity.switch_sides: Move the entity to the other side of its wall.
editor.tooltip.entity.wall_gap: How far off the wall the entity sits.
editor.tooltip.entity.snap_to_floor: Moves the entity down or up onto the floor it is in: the sector under it, and of that sector's floors the one nearest its height. Does nothing outside every sector.
editor.tooltip.component.decal.abs_heigh: When enabled, verticalPos is an absolute world height instead of a relative offset.
editor.tooltip.component.audio_source.so: Drag a .wav from the Asset Browser, or double-click one there and click here.
editor.tooltip.component.audio_source.re: Distance at which volume is at full gain.
editor.tooltip.component.audio_source.ma: Beyond this distance sound is inaudible.
editor.tooltip.component.audio_source.ro: How quickly the volume drops with distance.
editor.tooltip.component.script.file: Drag a .lua file from the Asset Browser, or double-click one there and click here.
editor.tooltip.component.script.open_fil: Opens this script in the script editor.
editor.tooltip.component.player_controll: Milliseconds before landing where a jump input is buffered.
Vertical offset from entity origin to the camera eye.
Whether this player controller is currently receiving input.
editor.tooltip.component.camera.fov: Vertical field of view in degrees.
editor.tooltip.component.camera.is_activ: Whether this camera is currently rendering.
editor.tooltip.component.collider.sphere: Sphere radius, multiplied by the Transform's Scale X.
editor.tooltip.component.collider.step_s: Max height, in world units, the collider can step up without being blocked. Not affected by the Transform's Scale.
editor.tooltip.component.collider.max_sl: Steepest floor, in degrees, the collider can stand on. On a steeper one it isn't grounded and slides down.
editor.tooltip.component.collider.capsul: Capsule radius: half its width. Multiplied by the Transform's Scale X.
Capsule height from bottom to top, rounded ends included. Multiplied by the Transform's Scale Y, and at least twice the radius.
editor.tooltip.component.collider.is_tri: Triggers detect overlap but do not physically block movement.
editor.tooltip.component.rigidbody.mass: Mass in arbitrary units. Must be > 0 for dynamic bodies.
editor.tooltip.component.rigidbody.gravi: Gravity multiplier (0 = floats, negative = repelled upward).
editor.tooltip.component.rigidbody.is_st: Static bodies are unmovable by physics but still collide.
editor.tooltip.component.model.file_name: Drag a model from the Asset Browser here. Its textures load automatically. The model is fitted to a unit box standing on the transform position, so Transform scale is its size in world units.
editor.tooltip.component.flipbook.file_n: Drag a .fpk flipbook from the Asset Browser here.
editor.tooltip.component.flipbook.sprite: Which of this entity's sprites the flipbook animates. The flipbook uses that sprite's side count.
editor.tooltip.component.flipbook.speed: Playback rate. 1 = the flipbook's own timing, 2 = twice as fast, 0 = frozen.
editor.tooltip.flipbook_editor.fps: How fast frames change. A frame with its own duration ignores this.
editor.tooltip.flipbook_editor.loop_mode: Once: stops on the last frame. Loop: starts over. Ping-pong: plays forward, then backward.
editor.tooltip.flipbook_editor.play_on_s: Starts playing as soon as the level starts. Otherwise a script starts it with Play().
editor.tooltip.flipbook_editor.frame_row: Click to show it in the preview. Drag to reorder. Double-click to rename. Right-click for more.
editor.tooltip.flipbook_editor.duration: How long this frame stays on screen, in seconds. 0 uses the flipbook's frames per second.
editor.tooltip.flipbook_editor.event: A function in the entity's scripts called when playback reaches this frame, e.g. Footstep. It gets the frame's name. Leave empty for no event.
editor.tooltip.component.camera.smooth_s: When active, the camera will smoothly step up/down the sector instead of abruptly teleporting
editor.tooltip.sector.add_floor: Adds another room interval above the current highest floor.
editor.tooltip.sector.remove_floor: Removes this room interval. A sector must contain at least one floor.
editor.tooltip.sector.invalid_floor_heig: The floor intervals overlap or the ceiling is not above the floor.
editor.tooltip.sector.floor: One vertical room interval inside the sector, defined by a floor plane and a ceiling plane.
editor.tooltip.component.transform.heigh: Vertical distance above the current sector floor, rather than an absolute world position.
editor.tooltip.component.transform.floor: The sector floor interval that the entity belongs to.
editor.tooltip.component.sprite.directio: Controls how many viewing directions use separate sprite images. Single uses one image, 4-Sided uses 90-degree steps, and 8-Sided uses 45-degree steps.
editor.tooltip.component.sprite.is_stati: If true, the sprite stays still instead of facing towards the camera
editor.tooltip.component.audio_source.pi: Playback-rate and pitch multiplier. 1.0 uses the sound's original pitch.
editor.tooltip.component.audio_source.ga: Volume multiplier for this source. 1.0 uses the sound's original volume.
editor.tooltip.component.audio_source.co: Makes the sound directional based on the direction the audio source is facing.
editor.tooltip.component.audio_source.ou: Volume multiplier used outside the outer sound cone. 0 = silent, 1 = unchanged.
editor.tooltip.component.camera.aspect_r: Ratio of viewport width to height, such as 16:9.
editor.tooltip.component.collider.type_b: Axis-aligned bounding box collider. Its faces remain aligned with the world axes.
editor.tooltip.component.collider.box_sc: Full size of the box collider along its X, Y, and Z axes, multiplied by the Transform's Scale.
editor.tooltip.component.rigidbody.frict: Resistance to sliding while the body is in contact with another surface.
editor.tooltip.component.ui_transform.an: Normalized lower anchor inside the parent UI element. (0,0) is bottom-left and (1,1) is top-right.
Normalized upper anchor inside the parent UI element. Separating it from Min Anchor stretches the element.
editor.tooltip.component.ui_transform.pi: Normalized point inside the element used as the origin for positioning, rotation, and scaling.

Top handle: rotate. {key:ui_nudge_up}/{key:ui_nudge_down}/{key:ui_nudge_left}/{key:ui_nudge_right}: nudge ({key:ui_big_nudge} for 10 px). {key:ui_duplicate}: duplicate. {key:ui_delete}: delete. {key:ui_undo} / {key:ui_redo}: undo / redo. editor.ui.arrange.to_screen: One selected - aligns to the screen
editor.ui.arrange.tooltip_distribute: Space the selected elements' centres evenly between the two outermost ones. Needs 3 or more.
&Context_NEW_1: Merge these keys into your existing English language file. Every other language file needs the same keys added too. &Context_NEW_2: The fixed world-space grid and its snapping toggles. Grid size is in world units and no longer changes with camera zoom.
editor.grid.title: Grid & Snapping
editor.tooltip.grid.size: Size of one grid cell in world units. This is also the snap interval, and it stays fixed no matter how far you zoom in or out. {key:grid_smaller} halves it, {key:grid_larger} doubles it.
editor.tooltip.grid.snap_to_grid: Snap new points to the grid.
editor.tooltip.grid.snap_to_points: Snap new points to existing dots and wall corners. Takes priority over the grid when both are enabled.
&Context_NEW_3: Shape-drawing tools used in Sector Mode. Each one draws a sector shape a different way. -Freehand- is the original click-out-a-chain-of-points tool.
editor.draw.title: Drawing Tools
&Context_NEW_4: Shown in the on-screen status overlay when Freehand is in -Manual Mode-, where only existing corners can be picked
&Context_NEW_5: A regular polygon: all sides the same length (triangle, square, pentagon, hexagon...)
&Context_NEW_6: A curved line, bent using a control point (a quadratic Bezier curve)
&Context_NEW_6B: Generates a run of adjacent sectors, each one step higher than the last, from a single dragged rectangle
&Context_NEW_7: Short one-line instructions shown under the tool buttons telling the user what to click next
editor.draw.hint.freehand: Click to place points. Click the first point again to close the shape.
editor.draw.hint.rectangle: Click one corner, then the opposite corner.
editor.draw.hint.polygon: Click the centre, then drag out a corner.
editor.draw.hint.circle: Click the centre, then drag out the radius.
editor.draw.hint.curve: Click a start point, then an end point, then a control point to bend the curve.
editor.draw.hint.staircase: Click one corner, then the opposite corner.
&Context_NEW_8: Number of sides on the polygon, e.g. 6 sides = hexagon
editor.tooltip.draw.sides: Number of sides on the polygon. Can also be changed with the {key:fewer_sides} and {key:more_sides} keys while drawing.
&Context_NEW_9: Button that sets the polygon side count to 6
&Context_NEW_10: How many straight line segments approximate the circle. More segments = smoother circle.
editor.tooltip.draw.segments: How many straight wall segments approximate the circle. Higher values look smoother but create more walls.
&Context_NEW_11: How many straight line segments approximate the curve
editor.tooltip.draw.subdivisions: How many straight wall segments approximate the curve. Higher values look smoother but create more walls.
&Context_NEW_12: Keyboard shortcut legend shown at the bottom of the Drawing Tools panel. {key:...} is replaced by the key the user bound (User Settings > Key Bindings) - keep those placeholders exactly as they are. Esc and Right-click are fixed and can be translated.
&Context_NEW_13: -Constrain- means holding Shift restricts the shape: forces a square, snaps the angle
&Context_NEW_13B: Ctrl temporarily ignores the grid for every drawing tool and while dragging wall geometry, not just Staircase
&Context_NEW_13C: Staircase-specific versions of the Shift/Alt shortcut lines, shown only while the Staircase tool is active
&Context_NEW_14: Button label for creating a sector out of hand-picked existing corners. Its tooltip key (editor.manual_sector.tooltip.create) already exists in your file.
&Context_NEW_15: Words shown in the small status overlay drawn in the top-left corner of the map viewport, next to the grid size number
&Context_NEW_16: Short measurement labels drawn next to the shape being created and in the status overlay. These sit beside a number, e.g. -R 40.0- or -Area: 360.0-. Keep them short; they are drawn over the map. -R- is an abbreviation for radius.
&Context_NEW_17: The length of one side of the polygon
&Context_NEW_20: Follows a number, e.g. -3 points-, counting points placed so far
&Context_NEW_21: The length of the edge that would be created by clicking right now
&Context_NEW_22: A chord is the straight-line distance between the curve's start and end points
&Context_NEW_22B: Follows a number, e.g. -4 steps-, showing the staircase's calculated step count
&Context_NEW_22C: Precedes the starting -> final floor height numbers, e.g. -floor: 0.0 -> 24.0-
&Context_NEW_23: Prompts shown in place of a measurement when the tool is waiting for its first click
editor.draw.prompt.first_corner: Click to place the first corner
editor.draw.prompt.curve_start: Click to place the start point
editor.draw.prompt.curve_end: click to place the end point
&Context_NEW_24: Error toasts shown when a shape is rejected and no geometry is created
editor.draw.error.min_corners: Shape needs at least 3 distinct corners.
editor.draw.error.min_points: Shape needs at least 2 distinct points.
&Context_NEW_25: The outline of the shape crosses over itself, which cannot become a valid sector
editor.draw.error.rectangle_zero_size: Rectangle must have non-zero width and height.
editor.draw.error.curve_same_point: The curve's start and end points must be different.
&Context_NEW_26: Staircase tool: settings panel shown when it is the active drawing tool. It generates a run of adjacent sectors from one dragged rectangle, each one step higher than the last.
&Context_NEW_27: Step Height mode: the user types the height and length of one step, and the step count is worked out from the size of the drawn rectangle
&Context_NEW_28: Target Height mode: the user types the length of one step and the floor height the top step should reach; the step height needed to get there evenly is worked out automatically
&Context_NEW_29: Step Count mode: the user types how many steps and how tall each one is; the length of one step is worked out by dividing the rectangle evenly
editor.tooltip.staircase.calc_mode.step_: You choose the step height and step length; the number of steps is worked out from the size of the rectangle you draw.
editor.tooltip.staircase.calc_mode.targe: You choose the step length and the floor height the top step should reach; the step height is worked out automatically so the last step lands exactly on that target.
editor.tooltip.staircase.calc_mode.step_: You choose exactly how many steps and how tall each one is; the length of one step is worked out by dividing the rectangle evenly.
editor.tooltip.staircase.step_height: Height gained per step. Can be negative to build stairs going down.
editor.tooltip.staircase.step_length: Length of one step along the direction the staircase is drawn. The last step is shortened to fit the rectangle instead of overshooting it.
editor.tooltip.staircase.target_floor_he: Floor height the final step should reach. Can be below the starting floor height to build stairs going down.
editor.tooltip.staircase.step_count: Exact number of steps to generate. Must be at least 1.
&Context_NEW_30: Which way the staircase climbs - Horizontal follows the rectangle's width (world X), Vertical follows its height (world Z)
editor.tooltip.staircase.direction.horiz: The staircase climbs along the rectangle's width (world X axis).
editor.tooltip.staircase.direction.verti: The staircase climbs along the rectangle's height (world Z axis).
editor.tooltip.staircase.raise_ceiling: When enabled, each step's ceiling rises by the same amount as its floor, keeping headroom constant. When disabled, every step keeps the starting ceiling height.
&Context_NEW_29B: Checkbox mirroring the Alt key - both flip the same setting, which decides which end of the drawn rectangle becomes the bottom step
editor.tooltip.staircase.reverse_rise: Flips which end of the drawn rectangle is the bottom of the stairs. Same as pressing {key:flip_staircase}.
&Context_NEW_31: Section header above the calculated step count/height/length/floor values, shown once a staircase rectangle is being drawn
editor.staircase.results.title: Preview
&Context_NEW_32: Staircase validation errors, shown in the settings panel and as a toast if a click is rejected. %d/%d in the step-limit message are the calculated step count and the maximum allowed - keep both in your translation.
editor.staircase.error.rectangle_invalid: Staircase rectangle corners must be finite.
editor.staircase.error.step_length_inval: Step Length must be greater than zero.
editor.staircase.error.step_height_inval: Step Height must be a finite number.
editor.staircase.error.target_height_inv: Target Floor Height must be a finite number.
editor.staircase.error.step_count_invali: Step Count must be at least 1.
editor.staircase.error.calculation_inval: Staircase calculation produced a non-finite value. Check the step settings.
editor.staircase.error.too_many_steps: Too many steps (%d, limit %d). Increase Step Length or reduce Step Count.
&Context_NEW_33: Non-blocking notices shown under the calculated values - the staircase can still be created
editor.staircase.notice.target_single_st: Target Height needs at least 2 steps to produce a rise. This single step stays at the starting floor height.
editor.staircase.warning.headroom: One or more steps have zero or negative headroom. Enable Raise Ceiling or lower the step height.
editor.geometry.title: Wall Editing
editor.geometry.hint.select: Click a wall to select it and open its inspector. Click empty space to deselect.
editor.geometry.hint.drag: Drag a wall to move it, or drag a square handle to move that endpoint. Connected walls follow shared corners.
editor.geometry.hint.delete: {key:multi_select}/{key:range_select} click to multi-select ({key:multi_select}+right click works too). {key:delete} removes the selected walls.
editor.entity_mode.title: Entity Editing
editor.entity_mode.hint.create: Press {key:place_entity} to place the palette's selection under the cursor.
editor.entity_mode.hint.edit: Right click an entity to open its inspector. {key:multi_select}+right click to edit several together.
editor.entity_mode.hint.move: Drag an entity with the left mouse button to move it. Dragging one entity in a selection moves all of them.
editor.entity_mode.hint.gizmo: Drag the red or blue arrow to move along X or Z, or the green square to move freely. Both snap to the grid; hold {key:disable_snap} to ignore it.
editor.entity_mode.hint.select: {key:multi_select}/{key:range_select} click to multi-select. Click empty space to deselect. {key:delete} removes the selected entities.
editor.entity_mode.hint.copy: {key:copy_entities} copies the selected entities, {key:paste_entities} pastes them at the cursor.
editor.entity_mode.hint.focus: Press {key:focus_selection} to center the view on the selection.
editor.tooltip.filters: Untick to hide this kind from picking. Hidden ones are drawn faintly and can't be clicked or dragged. Resets when the editor restarts.
editor.tooltip.geometry.split: Splits each selected wall in half. {key:split_wall}+click a wall to split it at the cursor instead.
editor.geometry.split_nothing: Nothing to split: the walls are too short.
editor.geometry.split_too_close: Too close to the end of the wall to split there.
editor.tooltip.geometry.merge: Joins selected walls that continue each other in a straight line, with the same sectors on each side and no other wall at the shared corner. The first wall's properties are kept.
editor.geometry.merge_nothing: Nothing to merge: the selected walls don't continue each other.
editor.tooltip.geometry.batch: Writes the ticked values to every selected wall. Unticked values are left alone.
editor.tooltip.geometry.align.chain: Starts at the wall you clicked last and follows the connected selected walls, so the texture continues across each corner. Walls running the other way get Flip X. Vertical offsets are copied from the first wall.
editor.geometry.align.chain_nothing: No selected wall connects to the first one.
editor.tooltip.geometry.align.reset: Sets the top and bottom texture offsets of the selected walls to 0.
editor.tooltip.geometry.align.fit: Sets the vertical texture scale so the texture fits the tallest visible part of the wall exactly once, and the vertical offset to 0. Horizontal scale is unchanged.
editor.geometry.align.fit_nothing: None of the selected walls has a visible part to fit.
editor.geometry.hint.split: {key:split_wall}+click a wall to split it at the cursor (snaps to the grid; hold {key:disable_snap} to ignore it).
editor.tooltip.entity_mode.palette.refre: Looks for .prefab files under Assets again.
runtime_editor.tooltip.palette: What {key:rt_place_entity} places: an empty entity or a prefab. Shared with the map editor's Entity Mode palette.
runtime_editor.palette.hint: Pick what to place, then press {key:rt_place_entity} while pointing at a surface or an entity.
editor.entity_mode.palette.hint: Pick what to place, then press {key:place_entity} over the canvas. Prefabs can also be dragged onto the canvas.
editor.entity_mode.palette.place_failed: Could not place the selected prefab. Check the logs.
editor.tooltip.entity_mode.placement.on_: New entities stand on the floor of the sector under the cursor. Off, they are placed at height 0.
editor.tooltip.entity_mode.placement.ran: Turns each new entity to a random direction around the vertical axis.
editor.tooltip.entity_mode.placement.tag: A project tag every new entity gets. Leave empty for none.
editor.entity_mode.placement.tag_unknown: No project tag has this name; add it under Project Settings > Tags.
editor.tooltip.entity_mode.align: Lines the selection up on the lowest, middle or highest value of the selection on that axis.
editor.tooltip.entity_mode.distribute: Spaces the selection evenly between its two outermost entities on that axis. Needs 3 or more.
editor.tooltip.entity_mode.snap: Moves each selected entity to the nearest grid point. Height is kept.
editor.tooltip.entity_mode.drop: Puts each selected entity on the floor of the sector it is in.
editor.tooltip.entity_mode.make_prefab: Saves each selected entity as its own .prefab in Assets/Prefabs, named after the entity, and links the entity to it.
editor.entity_mode.make_prefab_failed: Could not create the prefab. Check the logs.
editor.tooltip.entity_mode.filter.select: Selects every entity of this kind.
editor.tooltip.project.ui_reference_heig: Window height that UI Text Font Sizes are given at. Text is drawn at Font Size x window height / this.
editor.project.ui_reference_height_faile: Could not save the UI Reference Height to project.tilky. Check the logs.
editor.tooltip.project.texels_per_unit: Texture pixels per world unit at texture scale 1. A texture covers its pixel size / this, so it keeps its shape. At 4, a 128px wall texture is 32 units tall.
editor.project.texels_per_unit_failed: Could not save Texels Per Unit to project.tilky. Check the logs.
tags.none_available: No more tags. Create them in Project Settings.
tags.tooltip.delete: Delete this tag from the project. Removes it from every sector, wall and entity that has it.
tags.notification.duplicate_name: A tag with that name already exists.
tags.notification.save_failed: Failed to save project settings. Check logs.
editor.tooltip.tag_delete: Remove this tag from here. The tag itself is not deleted from the project.
editor.tooltip.sector.add_script: Attach a Lua script to this sector. The script gets a `sector` global that refers to this sector.
editor.tooltip.sector.remove_script: Detach this script from the sector.
editor.tooltip.sector.parent: Drag a sector here from the hierarchy, or pick one from the list. When the parent's values change, this sector's values change by the same amount.
sector.parent_cycle_error: Can't use this sector as the parent: it is this sector or one of its children.
editor.tooltip.user_settings.ui_design: How the editor's panels and menus look. Press Save to keep it for next time.
editor.tooltip.user_settings.texture_fie: Size in pixels of the texture previews in the wall and sector inspectors.
editor.tooltip.user_settings.runtime_cam: Field of view of the runtime editor's camera, in degrees. Only affects the editor view, not the game's cameras.
editor.tooltip.user_settings.remember_ca: On: the runtime editor opens where its camera was last left. Off: it opens at the mouse's position in the 2D view, at eye height above the floor there.
